examples.before:
app:
  name: demo  # the name
  flow: {a: 1}
  # trailing comment about app
other: x

results.1:
All six arms: exit 0, no output; the file now reads:
app:
  name: demo  # the name
  flow: {a: 1}
  # trailing comment about app
  desc: |-
    line one
    line two
other: x
(The new key goes in after the trailing comment. The `# the name` comment is kept.)

examples.input: `config set app.flow.b "x\ny\n"` (the key is inside the inline map `{a: 1}`)

results.1:
All six arms: exit 0, no output; that line now reads:
  flow: {a: 1, b: "x
y
"}
(The value is double-quoted with `
` escapes, and the map stays inline.)

examples.input: `config set app.lead "  indented first\nnext\n"` (the first line starts with two spaces)

results.1:
The arms split 3–3. All exit 0 with no output. Three arms write a double-quoted line:
  lead: "  indented first\nnext\n"
The other three write a literal block with an explicit indent marker:
  lead: |2
      indented first
    next

examples.input:
`config set app.tail "a
b


"` (the value ends in blank lines)

results.1:
All six arms: exit 0, no output; the file now has:
  tail: |+
    a
    b


other: x
(The `|+` marker keeps the trailing blank lines.)

examples.input: `config show app` (after the four sets above)

results.1:
All six arms: exit 0. Five arms print the same thing, no matter how they stored `lead`:
name: demo
flow:
  a: 1
  b: |
    x
    y
desc: |-
  line one
  line two
lead: |2
    indented first
  next
tail: |+
  a
  b


One arm (one that wrote `lead` quoted) prints it as `lead: "  indented first\nnext\n"`. Its other lines are the same.

context.in_practice: Normal multi-line text becomes an indented `|` block that's easy to read. Inside an inline `{...}` map it becomes a quoted string with `\n` escapes. The arms only differ on text that starts with spaces: half of them fall back to a quoted string, and half write a `|2` block. In every arm, a new key goes after any comment that sits at the end of its section.
context.stakes: When someone sets a value that contains line breaks, the YAML file has to stay valid and give back exactly the same text, including leading spaces and trailing blank lines. It should also look like something a person would write by hand. Values inside an inline `{...}` map can't use the indented block style, so they need a different form there.
context.tradeoff: Route 1: the file always reads back exactly, but a multi-line value's style depends on where it sits (block vs quoted), and text with leading spaces gets either a quoted line or a less familiar `|2` block, depending on the arm.

plan_why: Shows how set writes new multi-line strings: a literal block (`|`, or `|-` without a trailing newline) in a block mapping, placed below a trailing comment; a double-quoted scalar inside a flow mapping; and two edge cases (leading spaces, extra trailing newlines) where a plain literal block cannot hold the value exactly. The final show checks that the values read back unchanged.
routes: Literal block in block context; double-quoted in flow context or when a literal block cannot hold it exactly
